title: I teach calculus at Berkeley. Some of my students can’t do middle school math
excerpt: Since the University of California abandoned the SAT and ACT, thousands of faculty say it’s admitting students who aren’t prepared for the coursework. Will UC listen?
content_html:
In March, two California families opened college admissions decisions that should make anyone who cares about higher education stop and think.

One student — I’ll call him Elias — was admitted to a top University of California engineering program. His family was thrilled though surprised. Math had been his weakest subject in high school, but they assumed the university had seen something they hadn’t.

Another student — Nadia — watched rejection after rejection arrive from UC campuses. One turned her down even though she had earned A’s there in Calculus II and other college-level STEM courses through concurrent enrollment.

These are real students. I’ve changed their names, and withheld their schools, to protect their privacy.

Seen side by side, their outcomes don’t make sense. They make perfect sense only if you imagine admissions working less like careful evaluation and more like chance.

I don’t use that comparison lightly.

I teach mathematics at UC Berkeley. Three days a week, I stand in front of lecture halls with 500 to 1,400 students. By the second week of the semester, I already know who is in trouble. Some students are five to eight years behind in mathematics. Office hours that should be spent discussing integrals instead become lessons on fractions and basic algebra you would expect students to learn in middle school.

That is why this spring and summer, thousands of faculty members across all 10 UC campuses — including more than two-thirds of UC’s mathematics faculty — signed open letters (opens in new tab) urging the system to restore the SAT and ACT in admissions. Five Nobel laureates joined us, along with professors from across the university, including Beatriz Manz, Berkeley’s first Latina full professor.

We did so because what an admission letter is supposed to mean — that a student is ready to attend the school — no longer matches what we see in our classrooms. 

The math collapse

This isn’t a new debate.

In January 2020, a UC task force (opens in new tab) studied standardized testing and recommended keeping it. Then-President Janet Napolitano nevertheless urged the Board of Regents to phase out the SAT and ACT, citing pandemic disruptions and long-standing equity concerns. The regents voted that May to make testing optional, and a court ruling (opens in new tab) later that year, focused on access for students with disabilities, required UC to become completely test-blind through 2025. 

Since then, admissions officers have been forbidden from considering the one standardized measure that provided a common academic benchmark across California’s thousands of high schools.

Many peer universities have since reconsidered. MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Yale all suspended testing requirements during the pandemic. All have reinstated them. Across the Ivy League, similar reversals are underway.

UC has moved in the opposite direction.

Faculty asked the university to revisit the policy quickly, but the timeline has repeatedly slipped. The Academic Senate now plans a review that will conclude in June 2027, meaning no new admissions policy could take effect before fall 2028.

Students don’t have that kind of time: They attend college once!

The reason so many faculty have spoken out isn’t philosophical. It’s because of what the data — and our classrooms — show.

Before 2020, Berkeley administered a diagnostic exam to incoming Calculus I students. Between 2018 and 2020, 71% of roughly 2,200 students tested as ready or nearly ready for calculus. At the bottom of the distribution there was almost nobody. Just 0.14% tested below basic algebra.

After UC adopted test-blind admissions, the picture changed dramatically.

Berkeley Calculus I readiness, before and after test-blind admissions

Among approximately 2,800 Calculus I students tested between 2021 and 2023 with a different diagnostic that measured proficiency in eight mathematical topics, the share who were ready or nearly ready for calculus (meaning, they had proficiency in five to eight subjects) fell to 51%, dropping to 44% by 2023. Most troubling, the bottom of the distribution exploded. Seventeen percent of students answered none of the eight diagnostic topics correctly. By 2022-23, more than one-third had severe math deficits, and the single most common score on the exam was zero.

The classroom itself changed shape.

Before 2020, most students clustered toward the “ready” end of the spectrum, with only a tiny tail at the bottom. Afterward, the middle hollowed out, and the weakest students became the largest single group. We didn’t end up with one somewhat weaker calculus class. We ended up teaching two different classes in one lecture hall: one for students who were prepared for college calculus and one for students who needed remedial mathematics that nobody had scheduled.

That distinction matters because it has been misunderstood publicly. An Aug. 12 article (opens in new tab) in the San Francisco Chronicle said that in the pre-2020 readiness assessment, 48% of students who took the exam were prepared for Calculus I. The article said the faculty reported higher readiness for students admitted under the test-blind policy. But that is incorrect. Our analysis (opens in new tab) defined calculus-readiness as students passing seven or eight out of eight topics on the diagnostic exam. By 2023, that figure had fallen to 26%. More important than any percentage is the distribution itself. The crisis isn’t simply that readiness declined; it’s that the middle collapsed while the bottom became the largest group in the room. The Chronicle didn’t mention that. 

Nor is Berkeley an isolated case. Although Berkeley’s before-and-after diagnostics were not identical exams, UC San Diego (opens in new tab) — which used the same placement test before and after 2020 — has documented the same broad pattern. This is not one professor’s anecdote or one campus’ problem. 

Those of us teaching such courses don’t experience the consequences as abstractions. We watch students struggle through material they were expected to master years earlier. We pause lectures to reteach linear equations instead of expanding students’ understanding of differential equations.

The people arguing this test-blind policy on television, in committee meetings, and in politics do not stand in front of 700 students three times a week or grade a first midterm with a pre-curved D/F average.

We do.

The cost of waiting

In July, two dozen professors traveled to San Francisco for the UC Regents meeting. Some came from as far as San Diego. Each had one minute to describe what was happening in their classrooms.

Outside the university, school districts have begun acting on their own. On Aug. 6, the San Dieguito Union High School District voted 4-0 (opens in new tab) to urge UC to reinstate standardized math testing for STEM admissions and encouraged other California school districts to consider similar resolutions.

Jennifer Doudna, the Nobel Prize-winning Berkeley scientist known for pioneering gene editing, summarized the concern in a letter to the regents this summer.

“The test-blind policy was a well-intentioned experiment,” she wrote, “but the reality in our classrooms shows that it has failed.” Admitting students who are unprepared, she warned, “sets them up for discouraging struggle. … We cannot afford another cycle of administrative delay.”

That last sentence is at the heart of this debate.

Defenders of scrapping the SATs and ACTs blame COVID or AI for a broad decline in K-12 education. They say those are the only reasons UC students aren’t as ready for math — not the lack of standardized testing in admissions. 

Both those factors surely contributed. California’s K-12 math program isn’t a success story. In 2025, only 37% of students in the state performed at grade level (opens in new tab). 

But neither fully explains what faculty are seeing.

General learning loss would lower the entire distribution. It would not hollow out the middle while piling students up at exactly zero. Something else appears to be compounding the problem. Whatever the mix of causes, the problems at UC accelerated precisely when the system discarded the one standardized baseline it once had. Without standardized tests, admissions officers are flying blind, especially as grade inflation has made transcripts a weaker indicator of readiness, and artificial intelligence has made admissions essays a weaker signal of students’ work. 

It’s also worth remembering that students entering in fall 2027 were in fifth grade when the pandemic began. If, seven years later, many cannot reliably solve a basic inequality such as x² > 4 — a four-answer multiple-choice question that fewer than half answered correctly — then “pandemic learning loss” is no longer doing all the explanatory work.

UC has twice tried to build a replacement for the SAT and ACT. Twice it has failed.

The 2020 task force estimated that a UC-specific admissions test would take nine years to develop. Berkeley Senate leaders projected a cost of $100 million to $150 million (opens in new tab). A second effort examined California’s Smarter Balanced Assessment Consortium (SBAC) — a standardized test that evaluates public school students’ mastery of English and math. In 2021, the Academic Senate concluded (opens in new tab) it was “not appropriate as an admissions test” and would likely cost about as much as the SAT while reproducing many of the same inequities critics hoped to solve.

Yet even after those conclusions, BOARS — the UC faculty committee that oversees admissions — spent much of spring 2026 revisiting SBAC before internal opposition forced that effort to be abandoned and the regents imposed an accelerated review. 

Meanwhile, another admissions cycle passes.

Which brings us back to Nadia and Elias.

Both took California’s standardized math assessment as juniors in 2024. Both later applied to UC Berkeley.

Two real Bay Area high schools put numbers to this pattern. At (opens in new tab)Dougherty Valley High School (opens in new tab) in San Ramon, 432 of 756 juniors exceeded California’s math standard in 2024, as measured by SBAC. Of the school’s 542 Berkeley applicants that fall, 44 were admitted (opens in new tab) — an acceptance rate of 8%.

At (opens in new tab)Mission High School (opens in new tab) in San Francisco, 193 of 202 juniors did not meet the state math standard. Yet Berkeley admitted 34 of the school’s 76 applicants — a 45% acceptance rate.

Based on those figures, at least 174 Dougherty Valley students who exceeded the state benchmark were rejected, and a student with Nadia’s academic record would have been among them.

At least 25 Mission High students who failed to meet the benchmark were admitted, and a student with Elias’ academic record could have been among them.

Even accounting for students who did not take the state assessment, the disparity barely changes.

Today, Nadia is thriving at an out-of-state university and is on track to graduate in three years.

UCB’s own data (opens in new tab) suggest Elias has roughly a coin-flip chance of failing his first calculus course.

I don’t believe either student was well served.

Perhaps Elias would have been better off beginning at a community college before transferring to UC engineering once his foundation was stronger. Perhaps Nadia should have had the opportunity to build her career in the California university system she had already shown she could succeed in.

Instead, both lost something.

The irony is difficult to ignore. UC has tried to make SBAC a replacement for the SAT, yet its admissions decisions often run contrary to those state standardized tests, letting in more students who fail the SBAC. Without SAT or ACT scores — and without faculty input into the admissions criteria — UC’s process struggled to distinguish a student on the edge of failing calculus from one who had already excelled in college-level mathematics.

On the current schedule, no policy change could affect admissions before fall 2028.

That means every student applying until then will pass through the same system that produced Nadia’s and Elias’ outcomes.

Faculty have presented years of classroom evidence. Nobel laureates have spoken. School districts have begun passing resolutions. Yet the university’s response remains another study, another committee, and another delay.

The question is no longer whether more evidence is needed.

It’s how many more students we are willing to gamble with before acting.

Zvezdelina Stankova is a teaching professor of mathematics at UC Berkeley and recipient of the Mathematical Association of America’s Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award — the nation’s top honor for college math teaching. She is also one of the five original authors of the UC STEM faculty open letter urging the University of California to restore the SAT and ACT.

sentences.en: Since then, admissions officers have been forbidden from considering the one standardized measure that provided a common academic benchmark across California’s thousands of high schools.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，招生官员就被禁止考虑一项为加州数千所高中提供共同学术基准的标准化衡量标准。

sentences.en: In school year 2022-23, more than one-third of Calculus I students tested had severe math deficits. | Source: Sean Fan/The Standard
sentences.zh: 在 2022-23 学年，超过三分之一的接受微积分 I 测试的学生存在严重的数学缺陷。 |资料来源：肖恩·范/标准

blocks.html_en: Many peer universities have since reconsidered. MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Yale all suspended testing requirements during the pandemic. All have reinstated them. Across the Ivy League, similar reversals are underway.

sentences.en: Many peer universities have since reconsidered.
sentences.zh: 此后，许多同行大学都重新考虑了这一点。

sentences.en: MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Yale all suspended testing requirements during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 麻省理工学院、斯坦福大学、哈佛大学和耶鲁大学在大流行期间都暂停了测试要求。

sentences.en: All have reinstated them.
sentences.zh: 所有人都已恢复它们。

sentences.en: Across the Ivy League, similar reversals are underway.
sentences.zh: 在整个常春藤盟校，类似的逆转正在发生。

blocks.html_en: UC has moved in the opposite direction.

sentences.en: UC has moved in the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: UC 却朝着相反的方向发展。

blocks.html_en: Faculty asked the university to revisit the policy quickly, but the timeline has repeatedly slipped. The Academic Senate now plans a review that will conclude in June 2027, meaning no new admissions policy could take effect before fall 2028.

sentences.en: Faculty asked the university to revisit the policy quickly, but the timeline has repeatedly slipped.
sentences.zh: 教师们要求大学迅速重新审视该政策，但时间表一再推迟。

sentences.en: The Academic Senate now plans a review that will conclude in June 2027, meaning no new admissions policy could take effect before fall 2028.
sentences.zh: 学术参议院目前计划进行一次审查，将于 2027 年 6 月结束，这意味着新的招生政策不会在 2028 年秋季之前生效。

blocks.html_en: Students don’t have that kind of time: They attend college once!

sentences.en: Students don’t have that kind of time: They attend college once!
sentences.zh: 学生们没有这样的时间：他们上过一次大学！

blocks.html_en: The reason so many faculty have spoken out isn’t philosophical. It’s because of what the data — and our classrooms — show.

sentences.en: The reason so many faculty have spoken out isn’t philosophical.
sentences.zh: 如此多的教师发声的原因并不是哲学上的。

sentences.en: It’s because of what the data — and our classrooms — show.
sentences.zh: 这是因为数据和我们的教室所显示的内容。

blocks.html_en: Before 2020, Berkeley administered a diagnostic exam to incoming Calculus I students. Between 2018 and 2020, 71% of roughly 2,200 students tested as ready or nearly ready for calculus. At the bottom of the distribution there was almost nobody. Just 0.14% tested below basic algebra.

sentences.en: Before 2020, Berkeley administered a diagnostic exam to incoming Calculus I students.
sentences.zh: 2020 年之前，伯克利对即将入学的微积分 I 学生进行了诊断考试。

sentences.en: Between 2018 and 2020, 71% of roughly 2,200 students tested as ready or nearly ready for calculus.
sentences.zh: 2018 年至 2020 年间，约 2,200 名学生中的 71% 经测试已准备好或接近准备好微积分。

sentences.en: At the bottom of the distribution there was almost nobody.
sentences.zh: 在分布的底部几乎没有人。

sentences.en: Just 0.14% tested below basic algebra.
sentences.zh: 只有 0.14% 的人测试过基础代数以下的内容。

blocks.html_en: After UC adopted test-blind admissions, the picture changed dramatically.

sentences.en: After UC adopted test-blind admissions, the picture changed dramatically.
sentences.zh: 加州大学采用盲试招生后，情况发生了巨大变化。

blocks.html_en: Berkeley Calculus I readiness, before and after test-blind admissions

sentences.en: Berkeley Calculus I readiness, before and after test-blind admissions
sentences.zh: 伯克利微积分 I 准备情况，盲试录取之前和之后

blocks.html_en: Among approximately 2,800 Calculus I students tested between 2021 and 2023 with a different diagnostic that measured proficiency in eight mathematical topics, the share who were ready or nearly ready for calculus (meaning, they had proficiency in five to eight subjects) fell to 51%, dropping to 44% by 2023. Most troubling, the bottom of the distribution exploded. Seventeen percent of students answered none of the eight diagnostic topics correctly. By 2022-23, more than one-third had severe math deficits, and the single most common score on the exam was zero.

sentences.en: Among approximately 2,800 Calculus I students tested between 2021 and 2023 with a different diagnostic that measured proficiency in eight mathematical topics, the share who were ready or nearly ready for calculus (meaning, they had proficiency in five to eight subjects) fell to 51%, dropping to 44% by 2023.
sentences.zh: 在 2021 年至 2023 年间，大约 2,800 名微积分 I 学生接受了不同的诊断测试，该诊断测量了八个数学主题的熟练程度，其中准备或接近准备好微积分（意味着他们精通五到八个科目）的比例下降到 51%，到 2023 年下降到 44%。

sentences.en: Most troubling, the bottom of the distribution exploded.
sentences.zh: 最令人不安的是，分布的底部爆炸了。

sentences.en: Seventeen percent of students answered none of the eight diagnostic topics correctly.
sentences.zh: 百分之十七的学生没有正确回答八个诊断主题。

sentences.en: By 2022-23, more than one-third had severe math deficits, and the single most common score on the exam was zero.
sentences.zh: 到 2022-23 年，超过三分之一的人有严重的数学缺陷，而且考试中最常见的分数为零。

blocks.html_en: The classroom itself changed shape.

sentences.en: The classroom itself changed shape.
sentences.zh: 教室本身的形状也发生了变化。

blocks.html_en: Before 2020, most students clustered toward the “ready” end of the spectrum, with only a tiny tail at the bottom. Afterward, the middle hollowed out, and the weakest students became the largest single group. We didn’t end up with one somewhat weaker calculus class. We ended up teaching two different classes in one lecture hall: one for students who were prepared for college calculus and one for students who needed remedial mathematics that nobody had scheduled.

sentences.en: Before 2020, most students clustered toward the “ready” end of the spectrum, with only a tiny tail at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 2020 年之前，大多数学生都聚集在“准备就绪”的一端，只有底部的一小部分。

sentences.en: Afterward, the middle hollowed out, and the weakest students became the largest single group.
sentences.zh: 后来，中间被掏空，最弱的学生变成了最大的单一群体。

sentences.en: We didn’t end up with one somewhat weaker calculus class.
sentences.zh: 我们最终并没有上一门稍弱的微积分课。

sentences.en: We ended up teaching two different classes in one lecture hall: one for students who were prepared for college calculus and one for students who needed remedial mathematics that nobody had scheduled.
sentences.zh: 我们最终在一个报告厅教授两门不同的课程：一门是为那些准备大学微积分的学生开设的，一门是为那些需要补习数学但没有人安排的学生开设的。

blocks.html_en: That distinction matters because it has been misunderstood publicly. An Aug. 12 article (opens in new tab) in the San Francisco Chronicle said that in the pre-2020 readiness assessment, 48% of students who took the exam were prepared for Calculus I. The article said the faculty reported higher readiness for students admitted under the test-blind policy. But that is incorrect. Our analysis (opens in new tab) defined calculus-readiness as students passing seven or eight out of eight topics on the diagnostic exam. By 2023, that figure had fallen to 26%. More important than any percentage is the distribution itself. The crisis isn’t simply that readiness declined; it’s that the middle collapsed while the bottom became the largest group in the room. The Chronicle didn’t mention that.

sentences.en: That distinction matters because it has been misunderstood publicly.
sentences.zh: 这种区别很重要，因为它被公开误解了。

sentences.en: An Aug. 12 article (opens in new tab) in the San Francisco Chronicle said that in the pre-2020 readiness assessment, 48% of students who took the exam were prepared for Calculus I.
sentences.zh: 《旧金山纪事报》8 月 12 日的一篇文章（在新选项卡中打开）称，在 2020 年前的准备评估中，48% 参加考试的学生为微积分 I 做好了准备。

sentences.en: The article said the faculty reported higher readiness for students admitted under the test-blind policy.
sentences.zh: 文章称，教师们报告说，根据盲试政策录取的学生的准备程度更高。

sentences.en: But that is incorrect.
sentences.zh: 但这是不正确的。

sentences.en: Our analysis (opens in new tab) defined calculus-readiness as students passing seven or eight out of eight topics on the diagnostic exam.
sentences.zh: 我们的分析（在新选项卡中打开）将微积分准备就绪定义为学生在诊断考试中通过了八个主题中的七到八个。

sentences.en: By 2023, that figure had fallen to 26%.
sentences.zh: 到 2023 年，这一数字已降至 26%。

sentences.en: More important than any percentage is the distribution itself.
sentences.zh: 比任何百分比更重要的是分布本身。

sentences.en: The crisis isn’t simply that readiness declined; it’s that the middle collapsed while the bottom became the largest group in the room.
sentences.zh: 危机不仅仅在于准备程度的下降，还在于准备程度的下降。就是中间塌陷了，而底部成了房间里最大的一组。

sentences.en: The Chronicle didn’t mention that.
sentences.zh: 《纪事报》没有提到这一点。

blocks.html_en: Nor is Berkeley an isolated case. Although Berkeley’s before-and-after diagnostics were not identical exams, UC San Diego (opens in new tab) — which used the same placement test before and after 2020 — has documented the same broad pattern. This is not one professor’s anecdote or one campus’ problem.

sentences.en: Nor is Berkeley an isolated case.
sentences.zh: 伯克利并不是一个孤立的案例。

sentences.en: Although Berkeley’s before-and-after diagnostics were not identical exams, UC San Diego (opens in new tab) — which used the same placement test before and after 2020 — has documented the same broad pattern.
sentences.zh: 尽管伯克利分校前后的诊断测试并不相同，但加州大学圣地亚哥分校（在新选项卡中打开）——在 2020 年前后使用了相同的分班测试——记录了相同的广泛模式。

sentences.en: This is not one professor’s anecdote or one campus’ problem.
sentences.zh: 这不是一位教授的轶事，也不是某个校园的问题。

blocks.html_en: Those of us teaching such courses don’t experience the consequences as abstractions. We watch students struggle through material they were expected to master years earlier. We pause lectures to reteach linear equations instead of expanding students’ understanding of differential equations.

sentences.en: Those of us teaching such courses don’t experience the consequences as abstractions.
sentences.zh: 我们这些教授此类课程的人不会体验到抽象的后果。

sentences.en: We watch students struggle through material they were expected to master years earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们看到学生们努力学习他们多年前就应该掌握的材料。

sentences.en: We pause lectures to reteach linear equations instead of expanding students’ understanding of differential equations.
sentences.zh: 我们暂停讲座以重新教授线性方程，而不是扩展学生对微分方程的理解。

blocks.html_en: The people arguing this test-blind policy on television, in committee meetings, and in politics do not stand in front of 700 students three times a week or grade a first midterm with a pre-curved D/F average.

sentences.en: The people arguing this test-blind policy on television, in committee meetings, and in politics do not stand in front of 700 students three times a week or grade a first midterm with a pre-curved D/F average.
sentences.zh: 在电视、委员会会议和政治上争论这种盲试政策的人不会每周三次站在 700 名学生面前，也不会用预先弯曲的 D/F 平均分来对第一次期中考试进行评分。

blocks.html_en: We do.
The cost of waiting

sentences.en: The cost of waiting
sentences.zh: 等待的成本

blocks.html_en: In July, two dozen professors traveled to San Francisco for the UC Regents meeting. Some came from as far as San Diego. Each had one minute to describe what was happening in their classrooms.

sentences.en: In July, two dozen professors traveled to San Francisco for the UC Regents meeting.
sentences.zh: 七月，两打教授前往旧金山参加加州大学董事会会议。

sentences.en: Some came from as far as San Diego.
sentences.zh: 有些来自远至圣地亚哥。

sentences.en: Each had one minute to describe what was happening in their classrooms.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有一分钟的时间描述他们教室里发生的事情。

blocks.html_en: Outside the university, school districts have begun acting on their own. On Aug. 6, the San Dieguito Union High School District voted 4-0 (opens in new tab) to urge UC to reinstate standardized math testing for STEM admissions and encouraged other California school districts to consider similar resolutions.

sentences.en: Outside the university, school districts have begun acting on their own.
sentences.zh: 在大学之外，学区也开始自行行动。

sentences.en: On Aug. 6, the San Dieguito Union High School District voted 4-0 (opens in new tab) to urge UC to reinstate standardized math testing for STEM admissions and encouraged other California school districts to consider similar resolutions.
sentences.zh: 8 月 6 日，圣地亚哥联合高中学区以 4 比 0 的投票结果（在新选项卡中打开）敦促加州大学恢复 STEM 招生的标准化数学测试，并鼓励加州其他学区考虑类似的决议。

sentences.en: More than two-thirds of UC’s math faculty, along with five Nobel laureates, have signed open letters urging the university to reinstate the SAT and ACT.​ | Source: Christina House/LA Times/Getty Images
sentences.zh: 加州大学超过三分之二的数学教师以及五位诺贝尔奖获得者签署了公开信，敦促该大学恢复 SAT 和 ACT。​ |资料来源：克里斯蒂娜·豪斯/洛杉矶时报/盖蒂图片社

blocks.html_en: Jennifer Doudna, the Nobel Prize-winning Berkeley scientist known for pioneering gene editing, summarized the concern in a letter to the regents this summer.

sentences.en: Jennifer Doudna, the Nobel Prize-winning Berkeley scientist known for pioneering gene editing, summarized the concern in a letter to the regents this summer.
sentences.zh: 诺贝尔奖获得者、伯克利科学家詹妮弗·杜德纳 (Jennifer Doudna) 以基因编辑先驱而闻名，她在今年夏天给董事会的一封信中总结了这一担忧。

blocks.html_en: “The test-blind policy was a well-intentioned experiment,” she wrote, “but the reality in our classrooms shows that it has failed.” Admitting students who are unprepared, she warned, “sets them up for discouraging struggle. … We cannot afford another cycle of administrative delay.”

sentences.en: “The test-blind policy was a well-intentioned experiment,” she wrote, “but the reality in our classrooms shows that it has failed.”
sentences.zh: “盲试政策是一个善意的实验，”她写道，“但我们课堂上的现实表明它失败了。”

sentences.en: Admitting students who are unprepared, she warned, “sets them up for discouraging struggle. …
sentences.zh: 她警告说，接纳没有做好准备的学生，“会让他们灰心丧气……

sentences.en: We cannot afford another cycle of administrative delay.”
sentences.zh: 我们无法承受又一轮的行政拖延。”

blocks.html_en: That last sentence is at the heart of this debate.

sentences.en: That last sentence is at the heart of this debate.
sentences.zh: 最后一句话是这场辩论的核心。

blocks.html_en: Defenders of scrapping the SATs and ACTs blame COVID or AI for a broad decline in K-12 education. They say those are the only reasons UC students aren’t as ready for math — not the lack of standardized testing in admissions.

sentences.en: Defenders of scrapping the SATs and ACTs blame COVID or AI for a broad decline in K-12 education.
sentences.zh: 废除 SAT 和 ACT 考试的捍卫者将 K-12 教育的普遍下滑归咎于新冠疫情或人工智能。

sentences.en: They say those are the only reasons UC students aren’t as ready for math — not the lack of standardized testing in admissions.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这是加州大学学生没有为数学做好准备的唯一原因，而不是招生中缺乏标准化测试。

blocks.html_en: Both those factors surely contributed. California’s K-12 math program isn’t a success story. In 2025, only 37% of students in the state performed at grade level (opens in new tab).

sentences.en: Both those factors surely contributed.
sentences.zh: 这两个因素肯定都有贡献。

sentences.en: California’s K-12 math program isn’t a success story.
sentences.zh: 加州的 K-12 数学项目并不是一个成功的故事。

sentences.en: In 2025, only 37% of students in the state performed at grade level (opens in new tab).
sentences.zh: 到 2025 年，该州只有 37% 的学生达到年级水平（在新选项卡中打开）。

blocks.html_en: But neither fully explains what faculty are seeing.

sentences.en: But neither fully explains what faculty are seeing.
sentences.zh: 但两者都没有完全解释教师们所看到的情况。

blocks.html_en: General learning loss would lower the entire distribution. It would not hollow out the middle while piling students up at exactly zero. Something else appears to be compounding the problem. Whatever the mix of causes, the problems at UC accelerated precisely when the system discarded the one standardized baseline it once had. Without standardized tests, admissions officers are flying blind, especially as grade inflation has made transcripts a weaker indicator of readiness, and artificial intelligence has made admissions essays a weaker signal of students’ work.

sentences.en: General learning loss would lower the entire distribution.
sentences.zh: 一般学习损失会降低整个分布。

sentences.en: It would not hollow out the middle while piling students up at exactly zero.
sentences.zh: 它不会把中间的部分掏空，同时让学生完全为零。

sentences.en: Something else appears to be compounding the problem.
sentences.zh: 似乎还有其他因素使问题变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: Whatever the mix of causes, the problems at UC accelerated precisely when the system discarded the one standardized baseline it once had.
sentences.zh: 无论出于何种原因，UC 的问题恰恰在系统放弃了它曾经拥有的标准化基线时加速了。

sentences.en: Without standardized tests, admissions officers are flying blind, especially as grade inflation has made transcripts a weaker indicator of readiness, and artificial intelligence has made admissions essays a weaker signal of students’ work.
sentences.zh: 如果没有标准化考试，招生人员就会盲目行事，特别是因为成绩膨胀使成绩单成为衡量学生准备情况的较弱指标，而人工智能又使招生论文成为衡量学生成绩的较弱信号。

blocks.html_en: It’s also worth remembering that students entering in fall 2027 were in fifth grade when the pandemic began. If, seven years later, many cannot reliably solve a basic inequality such as x² > 4 — a four-answer multiple-choice question that fewer than half answered correctly — then “pandemic learning loss” is no longer doing all the explanatory work.

sentences.en: It’s also worth remembering that students entering in fall 2027 were in fifth grade when the pandemic began.
sentences.zh: 还值得记住的是，2027 年秋季入学的学生在疫情开始时才上五年级。

sentences.en: If, seven years later, many cannot reliably solve a basic inequality such as x² > 4 — a four-answer multiple-choice question that fewer than half answered correctly — then “pandemic learning loss” is no longer doing all the explanatory work.
sentences.zh: 如果七年后，许多人无法可靠地解决诸如 x² > 4 之类的基本不等式（这是一个只有不到一半人正确回答的四项多项选择题），那么“大流行性学习损失”就不再承担所有的解释工作。

blocks.html_en: UC has twice tried to build a replacement for the SAT and ACT. Twice it has failed.

sentences.en: UC has twice tried to build a replacement for the SAT and ACT.
sentences.zh: 加州大学曾两次尝试建立 SAT 和 ACT 的替代品。

sentences.en: Twice it has failed.
sentences.zh: 两次都失败了。

blocks.html_en: The 2020 task force estimated that a UC-specific admissions test would take nine years to develop. Berkeley Senate leaders projected a cost of $100 million to $150 million (opens in new tab). A second effort examined California’s Smarter Balanced Assessment Consortium (SBAC) — a standardized test that evaluates public school students’ mastery of English and math. In 2021, the Academic Senate concluded (opens in new tab) it was “not appropriate as an admissions test” and would likely cost about as much as the SAT while reproducing many of the same inequities critics hoped to solve.

sentences.en: The 2020 task force estimated that a UC-specific admissions test would take nine years to develop.
sentences.zh: 2020 年工作组估计，加州大学特定的入学考试需要九年时间才能开发。

sentences.en: Berkeley Senate leaders projected a cost of $100 million to $150 million (opens in new tab).
sentences.zh: 伯克利参议院领导人预计成本为 1 亿至 1.5 亿美元（在新选项卡中打开）。

sentences.en: A second effort examined California’s Smarter Balanced Assessment Consortium (SBAC) — a standardized test that evaluates public school students’ mastery of English and math.
sentences.zh: 第二项工作考察了加州智慧平衡评估联盟（SBAC）——这是一项评估公立学校学生英语和数学掌握程度的标准化测试。

sentences.en: In 2021, the Academic Senate concluded (opens in new tab) it was “not appropriate as an admissions test” and would likely cost about as much as the SAT while reproducing many of the same inequities critics hoped to solve.
sentences.zh: 2021 年，学术参议院得出结论（在新选项卡中打开），它“不适合作为入学考试”，并且可能会花费与 SAT 一样高的费用，同时也会重现批评者希望解决的许多不平等问题。

blocks.html_en: Yet even after those conclusions, BOARS — the UC faculty committee that oversees admissions — spent much of spring 2026 revisiting SBAC before internal opposition forced that effort to be abandoned and the regents imposed an accelerated review.

sentences.en: Yet even after those conclusions, BOARS — the UC faculty committee that oversees admissions — spent much of spring 2026 revisiting SBAC before internal opposition forced that effort to be abandoned and the regents imposed an accelerated review.
sentences.zh: 然而，即使在得出这些结论之后，BOARS——负责监督招生的加州大学教员委员会——在 2026 年春季的大部分时间里都在重新审视 SBAC，直到内部反对迫使这一努力被放弃，董事会也实施了加速审查。

blocks.html_en: Meanwhile, another admissions cycle passes.

sentences.en: Meanwhile, another admissions cycle passes.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，又一个招生周期过去了。

blocks.html_en: Which brings us back to Nadia and Elias.

sentences.en: Which brings us back to Nadia and Elias.
sentences.zh: 这让我们回到纳迪亚和埃利亚斯。

blocks.html_en: Both took California’s standardized math assessment as juniors in 2024. Both later applied to UC Berkeley.

sentences.en: Both took California’s standardized math assessment as juniors in 2024.
sentences.zh: 两人都在 2024 年作为三年级学生参加了加州标准化数学评估。

sentences.en: Both later applied to UC Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 两人后来都申请了加州大学伯克利分校。

blocks.html_en: Two real Bay Area high schools put numbers to this pattern. At (opens in new tab)Dougherty Valley High School (opens in new tab) in San Ramon, 432 of 756 juniors exceeded California’s math standard in 2024, as measured by SBAC. Of the school’s 542 Berkeley applicants that fall, 44 were admitted (opens in new tab) — an acceptance rate of 8%.

sentences.en: Two real Bay Area high schools put numbers to this pattern.

content_html_zh:
今年三月，加州的两个家庭公开了大学招生决定，这应该让所有关心高等教育的人停下来思考。

一名学生——我称他为埃利亚斯——被加州大学顶尖工程项目录取。 他的家人虽然感到惊讶，但还是很兴奋。 数学是他高中时最薄弱的科目，但他们认为大学已经看到了他们没有看到的东西。

另一名学生纳迪亚 (Nadia) 目睹了来自加州大学校园的一次又一次拒绝。 尽管她通过同时注册在微积分 II 和其他大学水平的 STEM 课程中获得了 A 的成绩，但还是有人拒绝了她。

这些是真正的学生。 我更改了他们的名字，并隐去了他们的学校信息，以保护他们的隐私。

放在一起来看，它们的结果毫无意义。 只有当你想象招生工作不像仔细评估而更像机会时，它们才完全有意义。

我不会轻易使用这种比较。

我在加州大学伯克利分校教数学。 每周三天，我都会站在有 500 到 1,400 名学生的演讲厅前。 到了学期的第二周，我已经知道谁遇到了麻烦。 有些学生的数学成绩落后五到八年。 本来应该用来讨论积分的办公时间变成了你希望学生在中学学习的分数和基本代数课程。

这就是为什么今年春天和夏天，加州大学所有 10 个校区的数千名教职员工——其中包括超过三分之二的加州大学数学教师——签署了公开信（在新选项卡中打开），敦促系统在招生中恢复 SAT 和 ACT 考试。 五位诺贝尔奖得主以及来自整个大学的教授加入了我们，其中包括伯克利第一位拉丁裔正教授 Beatriz Manz。

我们这样做是因为录取通知书的含义——学生已准备好进入学校——不再符合我们在教室里看到的内容。

数学崩溃

这不是一个新的辩论。

2020 年 1 月，UC 工作组（在新选项卡中打开）研究了标准化测试并建议保留它。 尽管如此，时任总统珍妮特·纳波利塔诺仍敦促董事会逐步取消 SAT 和 ACT 考试，理由是大流行造成的干扰和长期存在的公平问题。 5 月，董事会投票决定将测试作为可选，当年晚些时候法院做出一项裁决（在新选项卡中打开），重点关注残疾学生的入学机会，要求加州大学在 2025 年之前完全实行测试盲法。

从那时起，招生官员就被禁止考虑一项为加州数千所高中提供共同学术基准的标准化衡量标准。

此后，许多同行大学都重新考虑了这一点。 麻省理工学院、斯坦福大学、哈佛大学和耶鲁大学在大流行期间都暂停了测试要求。 所有人都已恢复它们。 在整个常春藤盟校，类似的逆转正在发生。

UC 却朝着相反的方向发展。

教师们要求大学迅速重新审视该政策，但时间表一再推迟。 学术参议院目前计划进行一次审查，将于 2027 年 6 月结束，这意味着新的招生政策不会在 2028 年秋季之前生效。

学生们没有这样的时间：他们上过一次大学！

如此多的教师发声的原因并不是哲学上的。 这是因为数据和我们的教室所显示的内容。

2020 年之前，伯克利对即将入学的微积分 I 学生进行了诊断考试。 2018 年至 2020 年间，约 2,200 名学生中的 71% 经测试已准备好或接近准备好微积分。 在分布的底部几乎没有人。 只有 0.14% 的人测试过基础代数以下的内容。

加州大学采用盲试招生后，情况发生了巨大变化。

伯克利微积分 I 准备情况，盲试录取之前和之后

在 2021 年至 2023 年间，大约 2,800 名微积分 I 学生接受了不同的诊断测试，该诊断测量了八个数学主题的熟练程度，其中准备或接近准备好微积分（意味着他们精通五到八个科目）的比例下降到 51%，到 2023 年下降到 44%。 最令人不安的是，分布的底部爆炸了。 百分之十七的学生没有正确回答八个诊断主题。 到 2022-23 年，超过三分之一的人有严重的数学缺陷，而且考试中最常见的分数为零。

教室本身的形状也发生了变化。

2020 年之前，大多数学生都聚集在“准备就绪”的一端，只有底部的一小部分。 后来，中间被掏空，最弱的学生变成了最大的单一群体。 我们最终并没有上一门稍弱的微积分课。 我们最终在一个报告厅教授两门不同的课程：一门是为那些准备大学微积分的学生开设的，一门是为那些需要补习数学但没有人安排的学生开设的。

这种区别很重要，因为它被公开误解了。 《旧金山纪事报》8 月 12 日的一篇文章（在新选项卡中打开）称，在 2020 年前的准备评估中，48% 参加考试的学生为微积分 I 做好了准备。 文章称，教师们报告说，根据盲试政策录取的学生的准备程度更高。 但这是不正确的。 我们的分析（在新选项卡中打开）将微积分准备就绪定义为学生在诊断考试中通过了八个主题中的七到八个。 到 2023 年，这一数字已降至 26%。 比任何百分比更重要的是分布本身。 危机不仅仅在于准备程度的下降，还在于准备程度的下降。就是中间塌陷了，而底部成了房间里最大的一组。 《纪事报》没有提到这一点。

伯克利并不是一个孤立的案例。 尽管伯克利分校前后的诊断测试并不相同，但加州大学圣地亚哥分校（在新选项卡中打开）——在 2020 年前后使用了相同的分班测试——记录了相同的广泛模式。 这不是一位教授的轶事，也不是某个校园的问题。

我们这些教授此类课程的人不会体验到抽象的后果。 我们看到学生们努力学习他们多年前就应该掌握的材料。 我们暂停讲座以重新教授线性方程，而不是扩展学生对微分方程的理解。

在电视、委员会会议和政治上争论这种盲试政策的人不会每周三次站在 700 名学生面前，也不会用预先弯曲的 D/F 平均分来对第一次期中考试进行评分。

We do.

等待的成本

七月，两打教授前往旧金山参加加州大学董事会会议。 有些来自远至圣地亚哥。 每个人都有一分钟的时间描述他们教室里发生的事情。

在大学之外，学区也开始自行行动。 8 月 6 日，圣地亚哥联合高中学区以 4 比 0 的投票结果（在新选项卡中打开）敦促加州大学恢复 STEM 招生的标准化数学测试，并鼓励加州其他学区考虑类似的决议。

诺贝尔奖获得者、伯克利科学家詹妮弗·杜德纳 (Jennifer Doudna) 以基因编辑先驱而闻名，她在今年夏天给董事会的一封信中总结了这一担忧。

“盲试政策是一个善意的实验，”她写道，“但我们课堂上的现实表明它失败了。” 她警告说，接纳没有做好准备的学生，“会让他们灰心丧气…… 我们无法承受又一轮的行政拖延。”

最后一句话是这场辩论的核心。

废除 SAT 和 ACT 考试的捍卫者将 K-12 教育的普遍下滑归咎于新冠疫情或人工智能。 他们说，这是加州大学学生没有为数学做好准备的唯一原因，而不是招生中缺乏标准化测试。

这两个因素肯定都有贡献。 加州的 K-12 数学项目并不是一个成功的故事。 到 2025 年，该州只有 37% 的学生达到年级水平（在新选项卡中打开）。

但两者都没有完全解释教师们所看到的情况。

一般学习损失会降低整个分布。 它不会把中间的部分掏空，同时让学生完全为零。 似乎还有其他因素使问题变得更加复杂。 无论出于何种原因，UC 的问题恰恰在系统放弃了它曾经拥有的标准化基线时加速了。 如果没有标准化考试，招生人员就会盲目行事，特别是因为成绩膨胀使成绩单成为衡量学生准备情况的较弱指标，而人工智能又使招生论文成为衡量学生成绩的较弱信号。

还值得记住的是，2027 年秋季入学的学生在疫情开始时才上五年级。 如果七年后，许多人无法可靠地解决诸如 x² > 4 之类的基本不等式（这是一个只有不到一半人正确回答的四项多项选择题），那么“大流行性学习损失”就不再承担所有的解释工作。

加州大学曾两次尝试建立 SAT 和 ACT 的替代品。 两次都失败了。

2020 年工作组估计，加州大学特定的入学考试需要九年时间才能开发。 伯克利参议院领导人预计成本为 1 亿至 1.5 亿美元（在新选项卡中打开）。 第二项工作考察了加州智慧平衡评估联盟（SBAC）——这是一项评估公立学校学生英语和数学掌握程度的标准化测试。 2021 年，学术参议院得出结论（在新选项卡中打开），它“不适合作为入学考试”，并且可能会花费与 SAT 一样高的费用，同时也会重现批评者希望解决的许多不平等问题。

然而，即使在得出这些结论之后，BOARS——负责监督招生的加州大学教员委员会——在 2026 年春季的大部分时间里都在重新审视 SBAC，直到内部反对迫使这一努力被放弃，董事会也实施了加速审查。

与此同时，又一个招生周期过去了。

这让我们回到纳迪亚和埃利亚斯。

两人都在 2024 年作为三年级学生参加了加州标准化数学评估。 两人后来都申请了加州大学伯克利分校。

两所真正的湾区高中用数字证明了这一模式。 根据 SBAC 的测量，在圣拉蒙 (在新选项卡中打开) 的多尔蒂谷高中 (在新选项卡中打开) 756 名三年级学生中，有 432 人在 2024 年超过了加州的数学标准。 那年秋季，学校招收了 542 名伯克利分校申请者，其中 44 人被录取（在新选项卡中打开），录取率为 8%。

在旧金山 (在新选项卡中打开)Mission 高中 (在新选项卡中打开)，202 名三年级学生中有 193 名未达到州数学标准。 然而，伯克利大学录取了该校 76 名申请者中的 34 名，录取率为 45%。

根据这些数据，至少有 174 名超过州基准的多尔蒂谷学生被拒绝，而像纳迪亚这样的学习成绩的学生也可能在其中。

至少有 25 名未达到标准的 Mission High 学生被录取，而像 Elias 那样学习成绩的学生可能也在其中。

即使考虑到没有参加州评估的学生，这种差距也几乎没有变化。

如今，纳迪亚在一所州外大学里茁壮成长，并有望在三年内毕业。

UCB 自己的数据（在新选项卡中打开）表明，埃利亚斯在他的第一门微积分课程上失败的可能性大约是抛硬币的。

我认为这两个学生都没有得到很好的服务。

也许埃利亚斯最好先从一所社区大学开始，一旦基础更牢固，再转学到加州大学工程系。 也许纳迪亚应该有机会在加州大学系统中建立自己的职业生涯，她已经证明了自己可以取得成功。

相反，两人都失去了一些东西。

这种讽刺是难以忽视的。 加州大学曾试图让 SBAC 取代 SAT，但其招生决定往往与州标准化考试背道而驰，导致更多未通过 SBAC 的学生入学。 没有 SAT 或 ACT 成绩，也没有教师参与录取标准，加州大学的流程很难区分微积分濒临失败的学生和已经在大学数学方面表现出色的学生。

按照目前的时间表，2028 年秋季之前的政策变化不会影响招生。

这意味着在此之前申请的每个学生都将通过与纳迪亚和埃利亚斯的结果相同的系统。

教师们提供了多年的课堂证据。 诺贝尔奖得主纷纷发言。 学区已开始通过决议。 然而，大学的回应仍然是另一项研究、另一个委员会和另一次拖延。

问题不再是是否需要更多证据。

是我们在行动之前愿意和多少学生进行赌博。

Zvezdelina Stankova 是加州大学伯克利分校的数学教学教授，也是美国数学协会黛博拉和富兰克林·泰珀·海莫奖的获得者，这是美国大学数学教学的最高荣誉。 她也是 UC STEM 教员公开信敦促加州大学恢复 SAT 和 ACT 的五位原作者之一。
